topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The increased beam squint due to a 45° scan range leads to depolarization, reducing signal strength and increasing interference. This results in higher sidelobe levels (-11 dB) and decreased antenna gain, necessitating additional power or capacity to compensate for the decreased performance. The link budget implications are twofold: reduced signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to increased beam squint and depolarization, and increased bit error rate (BER) due to high sidelobe levels and reduced antenna gain.
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth on the effects of a 45° scan range on link budget calculations. It highlights the importance of considering beam squint, depolarization, and sidelobe levels in satellite communication systems.
